key_insight: SIM-PINN combines projection-based equation splitting, iterative coupling, and multi-stage neural networks to improve convergence and accuracy for incompressible Navier–Stokes equations.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets more reliable mesh-free fluid simulation by easing nonlinear optimization, pressure–velocity coupling, and spectral bias.
method: Split Navier–Stokes into linearized momentum and pressure Poisson equations, each solved by dedicated neural networks.
Couple the separate solves through projection-based inner iterations.
Use multi-stage momentum networks to progressively refine velocity at targeted frequencies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved convergence and accuracy on steady lid-driven cavity and unsteady Kolmogorov flows, without quantitative metrics.
watch_item: Computational cost and sensitivity to stage design and inner-iteration convergence criteria are not quantified in the abstract.
paper_title: Projection-based segregated, iterative, and multi-stage physics-informed neural network for incompressible Navier-stokes equations
